title: a directory find can list but not search is passed over in silence on macOS, so every walk but clean's reports a whole answer over part of the tree -- the syntax gate passes over a planted breach and the runtime digest names another runtime, at rc 0
body:
FOUND 2026-09-24 by critic-shell's second pass on 0139 v2, reviewing cc's build, and re-driven by cc. 0139 makes every find under lib/ and bin/ read its status and leave its error on stderr, and that is not enough on macOS: BSD find passes over a directory it can list but not search -- mode 0444 or 0644, or any directory the running user may read and not enter -- when it lies below the start point. It prints no error, exits 0, and lists nothing beneath it. So a walk that reads find's output whole with its status, as 0127 and 0139 make every walk do, still reports a complete answer over part of the tree: IN-AG-NO-SILENT-001's shape, at a mode 0139's fix does not reach. 0131's sixth pass met the same shape and fixed it in clean alone, with an -exec clause in _clean_roots that asks /bin/sh whether a directory missing a search bit can be read and not searched, prunes it and names it, so the scan goes partial. One walk has a detector and the rest have none (IN-AG-HIGHLANDER-001).

DRIVEN by cc, BSD find on macOS against GNU findutils 4.11.0, with a directory sub/ below the start point holding one file:
- sub/ at 755: both list the file, rc 0.
- sub/ at 000 or 0111: both print "Permission denied" and exit 1.
- sub/ at 0444 or 0644: BSD find lists nothing beneath it, prints nothing, and exits 0. GNU find lists the file.
- The start point itself at 0644 or 000 is loud in both, rc 1 with an error, and a walk bounded at -maxdepth 1 never enters sub/, so neither of those is exposed.
- runtime_digest, from 0139 v2's build, over a lib whose sub/ is at 0644: rc 0 and a2cb00c1c3fa, which is exactly the digest of the same lib with sub/ removed; with sub/ readable it is b1e0b7a6fc2c. The digest names a runtime that is not the one on disk, at rc 0 -- 0139's point 9 again.

DRIVEN by critic-shell on 0139 v2, reported rather than re-run by cc:
- `bin/devbin check syntax` with lib/zzprobe/bad, a file holding a syntax error, under lib/zzprobe at 0644: rc 0, "syntax: 47 file(s), 0 breach(es)" -- 0139's driven case 2 at another mode.
- `infra profiles` with locked/ at 0644 holding the second profile to claim x.example: rc 0, "1 profile(s) under estate, no domain claimed twice" -- 0139's driven case 1 at another mode.

READ, NOT DRIVEN: every other walk that descends below its start point, by function.
- shell_files, which feeds the syntax, lint and critic gates (bin/.devbin/cmd/.lib/shell-gate).
- infra profiles' search, at -maxdepth 3.
- find_list (0139 v2), and so check's Swift gate and dmarc parse.
- cargo_target_dirs, and so fullcycle's artefact check; 0139 v2's mode test there covers a tree and its two profiles only.
- new's test_dir, which picks where to scaffold.
- check autotests' crate walk.
- runtime_digest (driven above), and version_identity and fleet through it.
- _vendored_find in lib/install, and so vendored_paths: an install, an upgrade or a vendor over a source whose lib/ holds such a directory could write or compare a manifest short of the files beneath it.
- doctor's _check_unowned.
- fleet's find_installs and outside_roots, the census.
- seam_git_state's symlink scan in lib/install, which answers UNREADABLE only when find fails.
- check toolchain's OTP lookup, at -maxdepth 2 under releases/: a version directory at 0644 reads as absent, and the lookup falls back to the coarse comparison, which says it is coarse, though no error says why.
Not exposed: _notes_releases_versions, fullcycle's PATH watch and check autotests' two counts, each at -maxdepth 1, and devbin_update_notice's stamp check, at -maxdepth 1 with its errors dropped by design.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO. One detector, in lib/helpers, used by every walk that descends: a directory the running user can read and not search is named, pruned and makes the walk partial, exactly as a directory find cannot read does under 0139, and clean's clause moves into it, so there is one. It asks the running user's permission as clean's clause does, `[ -r ] && [ ! -x ]` under /bin/sh, with nothing found through PATH. Each caller reports the partial walk as it reports find's failure: a gate or a check fails, and a verb that acts may act on what it found and still exit non-zero. Its arms drive BSD's silence, the case that is silent, and hold that GNU, which lists the names, reaches the same verdict. A source arm holds that every descending walk under lib/ and bin/ uses the detector or says why not. Pages change where behaviour does.

cc's, filed on vc's ruling of 2026-09-24, into 0.1.8. It is built after 0131 and 0139 land, and its design goes to vc before the build. 0139's close states this gap and cites this issue.

## Resolution

Fixed at 8962ced. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. One detector, find_walk in lib/helpers, finds a directory the running user can list but not search -- mode 0444 or 0644 below a walk's start point, which macOS's find passed over at rc 0 with nothing said -- names it ("cannot search <dir> -- nothing beneath it was looked at"), prunes it, and makes the walk partial, under BSD and GNU find alike. Every walk that descends goes through it or through find_list, built on it: fifteen of them, clean's own clause folded in; a contract arm holds that, a bounded find carrying a `# find-walk:` mark saying why. A caller's own leading prune is asked first, so a .git it prunes is never examined; the exec runs /bin/sh named whole, only for a directory the running user does not own with its search bit, so an ordinary tree runs none; find's status survives errexit; the depth rule keeps a directory any start path would enter, counted from each; a -mindepth above 1 and a depth option with no value are refused.
- NOT CHANGED, ON THE RECORD. A directory whose ACL denies search, its mode bits allowing it, is not asked about (vc's ruling: declared on clean's page and in find_walk's comment). Where /bin/sh cannot be run, the walk refuses at status 2, with no arm, since /bin/sh cannot be taken away on a test host.
- REVIEWS. critic-shell's passes: on v1, 1 critical (an arm of this change failed on macOS, its lock on the start point) and 5 warnings, each built; on v2, 2 warnings (the owner read from an `id` through PATH; the owner half unpinned), built as v2b; converged. vc's review: vc, 2026-09-26, approved at v2c on the rulings built as ruled, the drives and the evidence below; the final suite over the landed stack is below.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. Each walk's 0644 half red at its own assertion on HEAD's code, each helper arm on the code before it. 35 mutants, each against its own killer: 34 killed; T1's dedup half killed by the two-spellings arm, its depth half equivalent on both finds here, neither re-spelling a start path (measured). Fleet's census walk, timed: 2.02s against plain find's 1.96s over the roots, 7.1s against 7.0s over $HOME; v1 took 6.25s and 14.4s.
- THE SUITE. All of tests/unit over the six remaining 0.1.8 changes stacked in landing order on a252178 (0134, 0135, 0145, 0149, 0148, 0150), on a clean checkout built from the six exports (head 55f4c7e, tree 840726e0, the build stack's own tree), 2026-09-26 02:11:38Z to 02:46:47Z: 2040 of 2040 ok, 0 not ok, its 5 skips the declared ones (two no-tty branches, two require_command arms that skip off CI, the case-sensitive rename arm on this case-folding disk); the arms that need real cargo ran. Main after the landing is byte-identical to that tree.
